title: Don't count environment stops toward the drain's repeated-failure rule
summary: The drain counts any failed attempt toward its two-attempt limit, so a rejection plus a "producer login expired" stop ends the run as "repeated failure". An attempt that ends in an environment stop will no longer count; the item stays queued and the run goes on. Audience: people who run the drain and read its stop reason.

defaults_applied.how: The change is Rust in athena-cli.
New drain test plus existing tests for the two-failure case.
The drain reuses the shared environment classifier and the other readers of the count are checked.
The criteria run the drain tests and check the run goes on to the next item.
The existing disk.rs classifier is reused instead of a new list.
One focused change in the drain plus a test and a changelog entry.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: `attempts` counts `failures` against ATTEMPTS and returns ItemEnd::Failed, which `set_stop`s Stop::RepeatedFailure; `run_job` turns any run outcome that is not passed, needs-accepting or held into RunStep::Failed, with the run's reason in `line.reason`. The environment classifier is `athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason` / `StopCause::of` in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs (PRODUCER_AUTH = "environment: producer login expired"), already used by crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs. The change reuses it and adds no second list. It adds no record or data file under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not involved.

Design: in `run_job`, a run whose reason is an environment stop yields a new non-failure step (like Held/Waiting), which `attempts` maps to an item end that leaves the item queued, notes the reason via pass_over and lets the run go on. Environment stops already reach this path with outcome Failed and a reason.

Readers of the repeated-failure count found by search: (1) `failures`/ATTEMPTS in Drain::attempts (the rule being fixed); (2) the Stop::RepeatedFailure display in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs and the report fields in drain.rs (read only after the stop is set; covered by the existing drain.rs tests the_same_item_failing_twice_is_a_repeated_failure_naming_the_item); (3) crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs `repeated_failures`, a per-class count of Rejected/Failed jobs fed to the steward, which also counts environment-stop jobs. The producer decides whether to exclude them there too, with a test, or records why not.
The goal (environment stops not counted) is in scope and is not an out_of_scope item.
No refusal rule is added; the change refuses fewer runs as repeated failure, not more readings.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs: an item whose first attempt is rejected and whose second ends with reason "environment: producer login expired" does not end the run with Stop::RepeatedFailure; the item stays queued and the drain goes on to the next item and works it. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain.

The existing drain tests the_same_item_failing_twice_is_a_repeated_failure_naming_the_item and a_job_that_does_not_land_twice_still_ends_as_repeated_failure_when_the_config_is_readable still pass: two real failures still stop the run. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain.
The drain decides an attempt is an environment stop by calling athena_core::disk::is_environment_reason (or StopCause); a Grep of crates/athena-cli finds no new list of environment reason strings.
The drain.rs module docs state that an attempt ending in an environment stop does not count toward Stop::RepeatedFailure and that the item stays queued.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry saying that environment stops (login expired, usage limit, low disk, network) no longer count toward the drain's repeated-failure rule.

The final report lists every reader of the repeated-failure count (at least drain.rs attempts, display.rs, steward.rs repeated_failures), each with a test or a stated reason; if steward.rs is changed, a steward test shows an environment-stop job is not counted.

out_of_scope: Changing the scope guard's own counting or the environment classifier's list in disk.rs
Changing how `athena retry` resumes environment stops
Reworking the drain's other stop reasons
Adding a repository-wide fmt, clippy or test run as its own criterion
urgent_reason: It cuts wasted runs: a drain stopped as "repeated failure" because of an expired login and was rerun for nothing.
hard_reason: It changes the drain's stopping rule (repeated failure), which decides whether a run is held or goes on.
